inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E (year ended 30 Sep 2026, unreported at valuation date): H1 FY2026 actual $24,983m (+10.7% reported) plus H2 at ~+10% on H2 FY2025's $23,502m (organic ~7% + Vermaat/Pro Care M&A + FX). FY2025 actual was $46,070m. Using FY2026E as FY0 keeps the end-of-year discounting honest: FY2027 flows are ~1 year from the valuation date.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares, H1 FY2026 interim note 5 (1,699m; basic 1,697m + 2m dilutive share plans). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks are the funding mechanism and are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_note: 31 Mar 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim, components of net debt): borrowings 7,490 + derivative financial instruments 24 - cash 523 = 6,991. Lease liabilities of 1,641 are EXCLUDED (lease treatment B: the lease cash cost is charged inside EBITDA). Company-defined net debt incl. leases is 8,632 (1.7x EBITDA, above the 1.0-1.5x target after Vermaat; management expects to return to range).
inputs.last_fcf_note: TTM to 31 Mar 2026. reported_fcf = OCF - capex = FY2025 1,982 + H1 FY26 781 - H1 FY25 750 = 2,013 (post interest paid, post lease interest, pre lease principal). last_fcf = 2,013 - SBC 88 - lease principal 301 - interest income 0 = 1,624: levered owner FCF after the full lease payment. The engine's projections are UNLEVERED (EBITDA -> tax -> capex) and so sit above this by after-tax net interest (~$220m).
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income $80m FY2025 ($37m interest received) left in flows: the company is a net borrower, so the cash earning it is already netted inside net_debt; no double count of a cash pile.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow note 'Share-based payments - charged to profit' $82m (FY2024 $68m); H1 FY2026 $46m vs H1 FY2025 $40m. No separate equity-award tax line disclosed (ShareAwardSettlement $17m H1 FY26 is treated as buyback-like, not added).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $115m (last tranche of the Nov-2023 programme); nil in H1 FY2026 while Vermaat ($1.6bn) and Pro Care ($270m) were funded. Flat count is partly funded, partly a modelling convention until buybacks resume.
inputs.fx_note: Statements in USD since FY2024 (1 Oct 2023). The LSE trading currency for the ordinary shares changed from GBP pence to USD on 1 April 2026; Yahoo chart meta reports currency=USD at inputs.price_as_of, 52-week range 26.00-35.23. So quote and reporting currency now coincide and no FX bridge is needed. Parity check: the USD quote divided by GBPUSD (~1.33, Oct 2026) lands in the low-GBP-20s, in line with the pre-switch sterling trading range. The GBP-era history (FY2019-FY2022) is NOT mixed with the USD series anywhere in this file; where a long CAGR is quoted it uses the FY2023 restatement rate (1.2216 USD/GBP, FY2023 underlying PBT GBP1,986m = USD2,426m).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.1% (Oct 2026) + 5.0% ERP x beta 0.85 = CoE ~8.35%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (S&P A / Moody's A2, EUR/GBP/USD bonds), ~3.4% after tax; weights ~88% equity ($53bn market cap) / 12% debt ($7.0bn ex-lease net debt). WACC = 7.75%, used in all three scenarios (risk lives in the flows, not the rate).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal + lease interest (FY2025: 265 + 77 = $342m, 0.74% of revenue; H1 FY2026 principal 161 annualising higher post-Vermaat) charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path = 0.80%; lease liabilities ($1,641m) excluded from net debt; D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: other intangibles 183 + contract fulfilment assets 338 + PP&E 407 = 928 = 2.0% of revenue; ROU depreciation 262 excluded).
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI book value $107m (FY2025 balance sheet) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI profit share is $12m/yr (0.6% of profit) so the flows are attributable within noise.
inputs.capex_note: Capex = intangibles + contract fulfilment assets + PP&E (FY2025: 347 + 492 + 545 = 1,384, 3.0% of revenue; FY2024 1,409, 3.4%). Management guides ~3.5% of sales for FY2026 on client mobilisation timing, 'slightly elevated'. Base holds 3.4% then eases to 3.2%.
inputs.tax_note: Underlying effective tax rate 25.5% (FY2025 and FY2024). Cash taxes paid: FY2025 653 / underlying PBT 3,020 = 21.6%; FY2024 693 / 2,749 = 25.2%. Cash rate modelled at 24% flat (bear 25%).
inputs.working_capital_note: Negative working-capital business (payables > receivables) but the net movement is small and noisy: FY2025 -40 on +4.1bn revenue growth, FY2024 +186 on +4.1bn. wc_capture set to 0 in all scenarios.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (scripts/dcf_engine.py via make build-dcf). Compass is a contract catering operating company (routing row: operating company, non-US), so owner-FCF applies with the adaptations file: USD WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-light market (0.18% of revenue, so house and street bands are close but not identical). FY0 is FY2026E because the fiscal year ended 10 days before the valuation date and is unreported; the balance sheet is the latest filed (31 Mar 2026). Price is a regular-session LSE print in USD, not after-hours. Horizon 10 years (FY2027-FY2036) so that margin progression has matured before capitalisation.

equity_bridge.note: FY2025 Annual Report balance sheet; charged once here, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management guidance: ~7% organic FY2026 (Q3 YTD 7.2%), net new business 4-5% for five consecutive years, medium-term 'mid-to-high single-digit' organic; year-1 base 7.5% incl. Vermaat/Pro Care carry-over, decelerating to 3% by year 10. Not the equity CAGR, which is inflated by USD translation and retained M&A goodwill.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (11%) exceeds owner-FCF CAGR (3.3% cc over 6 years; 17.8% over the clean USD 2-year window) by >30%: FY2019-FY2025 spans the COVID collapse (FY2020-21 revenue -28%) and the GBP->USD switch, so the long CAGRs are not a growth basis; the USD-only 2-year window is post-recovery and overstates.
historical_growth.notes: 3-year and 5-year CAGRs are deliberately null: the FY2022/FY2023 boundary is a GBP->USD reporting change and FY2020-FY2021 are COVID-trough years. 2-year CAGRs are on the clean USD-restated series (FY2023 restated in the FY2024 AR -> FY2025). 6-year constant-currency CAGRs convert FY2019 GBP at the FY2023 restatement rate 1.2216. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - lease principal (FY2019 is pre-IFRS16 so no lease adjustment): FY2019 GBP1,102m = USD1,346m; FY2023 1,179; FY2025 1,635. Owner-FCF growth (3.3% cc) is well below revenue (7.2%): IFRS16 reclassification, higher capex intensity (3.0% vs 3.3% pre-COVID) and higher interest paid absorbed part of the recovery.

base.narrative: Organic growth ~6.5% (net new 4-5% + pricing/volume) in FY2027 plus the last of the Vermaat/Pro Care annualisation, fading to 3% by FY2036 as first-time outsourcing matures. Underlying operating margin progresses ~10bps/yr from 7.4% (H1 FY2026) toward ~8% (EBITDA 10.55% -> 11.0% post-IFRS16, before the 0.8% lease charge). Capex eases from the 3.4-3.5% mobilisation peak to 3.2%.

bull.narrative: High-single-digit organic growth sustained (net new business at the top of 4-5%, record pipeline, AI data-centre and defence/energy niches, European platform M&A replicating North America) with margin reaching ~8.5% operating / 11.8% EBITDA through overhead leverage and GPO procurement scale.

bear.narrative: A US recession and return-to-office stall cut Business & Industry volumes, net new business slips below the 4% floor, labour and food inflation outruns contractual indexation and the Vermaat integration dilutes margin: operating margin drifts back to ~7% (EBITDA 10.0%), capex stays at the 3.5% mobilisation level and leverage above target keeps buybacks off the table. Terminal cap 16x FCF reflects a de-rated, slower-growth caterer.

scenario_narratives.base: Compass compounds as the scale leader in a ~$360bn, 75%-self-operated market: organic growth of 6-7% in the near years (net new business 4-5%, pricing ~2-3%, like-for-like volume ~1%) fading to 3%, operating margin progressing ~10bps/yr from 7.4% to ~8% by FY2032, capex normalising from the 3.5% mobilisation peak to 3.2%, cash tax 24%, leases charged as an operating cost at 0.8% of revenue, net debt from the 31 Mar 2026 balance sheet after Vermaat. Terminal growth 2.75% at a 7.75% USD WACC with the 20x FCF cap binding.
scenario_narratives.bull: First-time outsourcing accelerates (half of wins already), AI hyperscaler/data-centre, defence and Sports & Leisure niches add a point of growth, the European platform (Vermaat, Dupont, 4Service, Pro Care) delivers North America-style M&A returns and procurement/overhead leverage carries the operating margin to ~8.5%. Growth 9% fading to 3.5%, EBITDA margin to 11.8%, terminal growth 3.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Macro slowdown in the US (68% of revenue) and corporate occupancy weakness compress volumes; re-tendering pressure from Sodexo/Aramark and in-house reversals pull net new business below 4%; wage and food inflation outpace indexation; Vermaat integration and higher interest on $8.6bn of debt absorb cash. Growth 5% fading to 2.5%, margin back to ~7% operating, capex stuck at 3.5%, terminal growth 2.0% and a 16x exit cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% house default) because leverage sits at 1.7x after Vermaat, above policy, while the thin ~7% margin leaves little buffer against a US labour-cost or occupancy shock; bull 30% rather than 35% because the bull case needs the European M&A platform to earn North America-style returns AND margin to expand a further 100bps at the same time, two independent things going right. Base 50%: five consecutive years inside the 4-5% net-new target and 96% retention make the base path the well-evidenced one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Compass on unlevered owner FCF with SBC expensed (immaterial at 0.18% of revenue), the full lease payment charged as an operating cost (leases therefore out of net debt), NCI deducted once in the bridge, and a USD WACC against USD flows and a USD quote. The thesis is a long-duration compounder: ~96% retention and 4-5% net new business make revenue highly visible, so the valuation is sensitive to the discount rate and terminal multiple rather than to any single year. The 20x FCF terminal cap binds in base and bull, so the model is deliberately not paying for multiple expansion beyond today's ~25x owner-FCF market multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates (>60% of EV): a 50bp move in WACC or terminal growth moves value by roughly 10%
Leverage 1.7x net debt/EBITDA post-Vermaat (policy 1.0-1.5x); net debt of $8.6bn incl. leases rises further if M&A continues at the FY2026 pace of $2.4bn YTD
Operating margin of ~7.4% means a 50bp labour/food-cost miss is ~7% of profit
North America is 68% of revenue: US recession, return-to-office stall or healthcare/education funding cuts hit the largest sectors
Capex guided 'slightly elevated' at ~3.5% of sales on client mobilisations; if that is the new normal rather than timing, owner FCF is ~$100m/yr lower than base
Currency: USD reporting and USD quote since April 2026 remove the share-price FX noise, but sterling-based holders carry GBPUSD translation on both price and dividends
